concepts.title: Getting Started: Brainstorming and Idea Collection
concepts.definition: Beginning is the hardest part of essay-writing, so the chapter offers warm-up methods: brainstorming ideas in a group or alone on paper, asking questions about the topic, and collecting everything relevant before judging it. Quantity first, selection later.
concepts.key_idea: Draft nothing yet -- first flood the page with ideas, then choose among them.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb114.txt opening (difficulty of beginning, brainstorming, group ideas, putting down thoughts on paper)
question_patterns: why is beginning an essay difficult
in class 11 essay writing: what is brainstorming and how does it help
describe ways of collecting ideas for an essay topic
how does group brainstorming differ from individual brainstorming
what should be done with the ideas collected for an essay
prepare an idea list for a given essay topic

solution_steps.explain: Set judgment aside and list every idea the topic suggests -- group or solo, fast and unfiltered.
Interrogate it: what, why, how, for whom -- each question shakes loose new material.
Only after the flood, sort the ideas into usable and unusable for the essay's purpose.

concepts.title: Structure: Beginning, Middle and End
concepts.definition: A good essay is architecturally ordered: an introduction that catches interest and states the approach, a middle that develops the argument in orderly paragraphs each with one central idea, and a conclusion that gathers the threads and leaves a considered final impression.
concepts.key_idea: Introduction opens the door, body walks the rooms, conclusion locks up -- one idea per paragraph.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb114.txt structure sections (introduction, body paragraphs, one central idea per paragraph, conclusion, linking)
question_patterns: describe the structure of a good essay
in class 11 essay writing: what should the introduction of an essay achieve
why should each paragraph carry only one central idea
what makes an effective conclusion to an essay
how are paragraphs linked in a well written essay
plan the structure of an essay on a given topic

solution_steps.explain: Decide how to hook the reader and signal the essay's direction in the first paragraph.
Order the main ideas logically, one to a paragraph, with links joining each to the next.
End by pulling the strands together -- summary, implication or image -- without introducing new arguments.

concepts.title: Characteristics of a Good Essay: Unity and Coherence
concepts.definition: The chapter lists the hallmarks of a good essay: unity, where every paragraph sticks to the main subject and is clearly linked to it; coherence, where sentences follow a logical sequence; and full development of each point, as shown in the model essay on hobbies.
concepts.key_idea: Unity keeps every paragraph on the subject; coherence keeps the sentences in step -- together they make an essay read as one piece.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb114.txt later sections (characteristics of a good essay: unity, coherence, development; model essay on hobbies)
question_patterns: what are the characteristics of a good essay

solution_steps.explain: Read each paragraph against the title; anything not clearly serving the main subject must go or be justified.
Check that sentences follow one another logically, with linking words showing the connections.
Confirm each announced idea is actually developed with examples or reasons, as the hobbies model essay does.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Carry out a brainstorm for the topic 'The Value of Outdoor Games' and list the usable ideas.

solution_template.explain: List freely: fitness, teamwork, discipline, fun, fees, time, safety, screens competing for children's hours.
Keep fitness, teamwork, discipline and the screens contrast; drop the weak or off-topic items.
Each kept idea can head one body paragraph -- brainstorming has built the plan.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student's essay on pollution ends with a brand-new argument about electric cars in the final line. What does the chapter advise instead?

solution_template.explain: New arguments belong in the body, not the conclusion.
The conclusion should gather what has been argued, not open a fresh front.
Move the electric-car point into the body as a paragraph, and close with a gathering statement.
